newsitem.title: SWEDEN: James Capel says doubts recovery of paper industry.
newsitem.headline: James Capel says doubts recovery of paper industry.

text.p: HSBC James Capel said on Friday it was reducing its forecasts for the paper industry across the board and a recovery expected late this year and early in 1997 may not be realised.

"While destocking appears to have ended last April, we are concerned that the expectation of a recovery, in the fourth quarter of 1996 and into 1997, that is currently discounted in paper sector share prices may not be realised," it said.
Capel said in the report -- which announced a downgrade in Swedish forest group Stora to sell -- that it expected sector earnings next year to be worse than in 1996.
"We now expect earnings in the paper sector to be worse in 1997 than during 1996 and we are currently reducing forecasts across the board," Capel said in a statement.
Capel said a fine paper price recovery since May had been excessively sharp at around 22 percent year on year in Q2 and reflected restocking ahead of planned price increases.

"A 25 percent increase in existing European fine paper capacity over the next 18 months means that we aniticipate significant oversupply in 1997. We also expect global pulp production to outstrip demand in 1997," Capel added.

Capel said it expected European newsprint prices to fall further following a five percent decline in Britain, "as we do not believe the 25-30 percent premium over North American prices is sustainable." -- Simon Haydon, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1004
